name: spek
why: An acoustic spectrum analyser that shows the frequency content of a file, a simple but satisfying way to see sound.

brief.what_it_is: Spek is a free, open-source spectrogram viewer, according to its homepage, for GNU/Linux, Windows and macOS. It is an acoustic spectrum analyser: you point it at an audio file and it shows that file's frequency content, so you can see what the sound is made of. The scout note describes it as a simple but satisfying way to see sound. I did not confirm the supported input formats or the exact display details from a README.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives only the one-line description, Free / open source spectrogram viewer available for GNU/Linux, Windows and macOS, and does not state a problem or motivation in the author's words.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the platforms named on the homepage (GNU/Linux, Windows, macOS). I did not read a README or install docs, so I have no details on dependencies, configuration or first-run steps.
brief.standout: Spek is a small, single-purpose tool that turns an audio file into a visible spectrogram with no setup, which the scout note calls a simple but satisfying way to see sound. I have not compared it against similar tools, so I cannot say how it differs from them.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release date, version number or last-commit date, and I could not reach a repository. The homepage is a Substack-hosted page by Alexander Kojevnikov; that is the author's publishing channel and says nothing about the code's maintenance.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage. The fetch returned mostly page markup and a line of text that says the site requires JavaScript; the readable content is thin. My two guessed GitHub repository URLs both returned 404, so I could not read a README, and I have no commands, install steps or source link. The '90,000 subscribers' figure on the page belongs to the author's Substack newsletter and is not a measure of the project's users. Licence is not stated in anything I read.
quotes: Free / open source spectrogram viewer available for GNU/Linux, Windows and macOS.
